**Context:** Wrapping up the Baylor Athletics software & tech management document set (framework, workflow handout, exec summary) after feedback that §3's NCAA language read as dismissive, then running `/closeout`.

**Key Exchanges:**
- User confirmed status on five open threads: already replied to Kenny, approved the doc fix, approved the §3 rewrite, has a drafted-but-unsent inventory email to unit Admin leaders (sending Monday 8/17), and has already reached out to Micah for a meeting next week (targeting Tue/Wed).

- Assistant flagged tone risk on the Monday inventory email (must read as building forward visibility, not uncovering unauthorized purchases — the register Kenny has cut before) and offered a pre-send review.

**Decisions Made:**
- §3 rewrite: dropped "high-level by design," reframed NCAA guidance as expectations each institution implements per its own structure, and added a pointer to Appendix A's recommendation-to-section crosswalk — so the section Jon reacted to now ends by directing him to the mapping.
- Synced workflow handout step 1.4 to the framework ("they do not create a separate ITS workflow"); all three docs now agree on 1.4 and the NCAA framing.
- Versioning normalized to `..._ER_2026-08-14.docx/.pdf` (exec summary PDF was inconsistently `..._ES.pdf`); 08-12 companions archived to `_Archive/2026-08-12/` MD5-verified.

- A phrasing fix is rarely single-document — the same sentence lived in all three deliverables; check siblings before declaring an edit done.
- All paragraphs were single-run, which made in-place docx text edits formatting-safe.
- PDF uploads to the thread failed when sent two at once (~0.9 MB batch limit) but succeeded individually — batch size, not file corruption.
